title: Chapter 141 — Installation Problems
intro: The dishwasher leaks. The range is not level. The fridge doors hit the cabinet.

sections.title: Common Install Failures by Category
sections.content:
Dishwashers: water leaking from the supply line connection — usually a loose fitting or a washer that was not seated properly. Not sitting level — front legs need adjustment. Door hitting adjacent cabinetry — the installer did not check clearance before tightening.

Ranges: not sitting level — all four legs must be adjusted. Gas connection leak — requires a pressure test with soapy water at every fitting. Anti-tip bracket not installed — this is a code requirement for every freestanding range and the most commonly skipped step.

Refrigerators: door swing blocked by wall or cabinet — measure before delivery, not after. Water line leaking at ice maker connection — compression fittings need to be tightened properly. Unit not level causing door alignment issues — a bubble level takes 10 seconds.

Washers: excessive vibration from unlevel floor or shipping bolts not removed — shipping bolts are the number one installation miss on front-load washers. Drain connection leaking — drain hose needs to be secured at the right height.

Most of these are preventable with proper pre-sale measurement verification and competent installation.

sections.title: The 24-Hour Check
sections.content:
Ask the customer to check within 24 hours: Is the unit level? Are all connections dry — no water on the floor under or behind the unit? Do the doors open fully without hitting anything? Is it making any unusual noises — clicking, humming, vibrating?

A 24-hour catch is a quick truck roll to tighten a fitting or adjust a leg. A 2-week catch often means water damage to floors, cabinets, or the unit itself. The cost difference between a same-week fix and a two-week-later discovery can be thousands of dollars in property damage.

Send a text the morning after delivery: 'Hi [name], quick check — is everything running smoothly? Any water, noises, or door issues? Let me know and I will get the team right back if needed.'

sections.title: Repair vs Replace Decision
sections.content:
When to send the crew back: loose connection, leveling issue, minor adjustment needed, bracket installation missed. These are 15-minute fixes.

When to replace: persistent leak after a crew visit, damaged door or panel discovered post-install, unit not functioning properly out of the box. Do not make the customer endure multiple repair visits on a brand new appliance — replace it.

When to escalate to manufacturer: suspected product defect, repeated failures on the same model across multiple units, unusual noises or performance issues that the install crew cannot diagnose.

The customer should never feel like they are coordinating between your install team, the manufacturer, and a third-party service provider. You are the single point of contact. You coordinate everything. They wait for your call with the update.
